title: 70 TIMES 7: THE PERFECTION OF MERCY THROUGH CHRIST

sense.text:
“Never trust thine enemy.” Never. Not sometimes, not in some situations: never. Our people, from the slave ships till now, are still in denial, with the illusion that we can change the minds of our oppressors: if we feed them, work with them, get into relationships with them, the so-called white man will change. These people will spit in your face and smite you, and you still think you can change them.

Chud the Builder is the example: a man who goes around Tennessee, a carry state, with his pistol on him, harassing black men and sisters, calling them out of their names and calling them the N-word to provoke them to anger so he can shoot them. He recently shot a brother he was insulting. Yet a black woman who knew him from when he was the plug, selling weed in Clarksville, dapped him up and said he was one of us because all his friends were black. The same stupidity our people said about Bill Clinton. Notice the cross on her neck: that is what Christianity does to our people. It pollutes the brain with assimilation, integration and turn the other cheek nonsense, which is not biblical.

“For like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” That hatred is perpetual, which is what Deacon Malachi brought out in his class on why the nations hate us.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him.” He was cool back then; now he is out trying to provoke black people to anger. Thou shalt know “that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

Can a leopard change his spots? You cannot change Esau. Brothers and sisters, you cannot change them.

This is the Most High, Christ, speaking to Abram before his name was changed to Abraham: “Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years.”

The seed spoken of is through the line of Isaac. Abraham had other children, and those are not the children of God; the Apostle Paul expounded that in Romans the ninth chapter. For those coming out of Christianity, with one foot in Christianity and one toe in the truth: the other nations are not God's chosen people. They are not God's children at all.

This is not talking about America. This is ancient Egypt, where Jacob and the souls with him walked in. Our people do not learn; that is why we were in the wilderness forty years, a hard-headed people. So why did God bring this judgment on us? The sons of God mixed with the daughters of men.

precepts.why:
This is why we went into Egypt. “The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” The sons of God come out of Seth. Cain slew Abel, Seth replaced him, and the chosen came out of Seth's line.

“There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.”

“And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth.” That wickedness in verse 5 is the sons of God taking the daughters of men unto themselves, when the Most High said don't do that. “And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.”

So now we know why the Most High told Abraham to know for a surety that his seed would end up in Egypt as servants four hundred years. As the sons of God we broke God's laws, and he had to bring forth judgment. Rightfully so.

“Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” That is the lineage of the sons of God, from Adam through Seth.

Write that down, so the next time the question comes up of who the sons of God were in Genesis 6, you are not confused.

sense.text: “And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.” Joseph was in Egypt already because he was sold into captivity by his brothers. We are in Egypt serving hard bondage because, as the sons of God, we broke God's laws.

“And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly.” Like we do here in America. They call us the minority, but we are really the majority; it is when it comes to power, and the lack thereof, that they call us a minority.
“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”: a new kingdom over Egypt.

“Come on, let us deal wisely with them.” America is modern-day Egypt, and this is how America deals wisely with us now: they keep us in the ghettos, put certain stores and bad food around us, put us in areas to keep us at the bottom, and use think tanks to come up with propaganda and plots to keep us destroyed.

Above all, religion and politics. Those are the two main things Esau uses to deal wisely with God's people. Before we came into the truth, most of us were Christians, some Muslims, thinking the so-called white man was Jesus, God is white, the angels are white, confused in all these denominations that kept us from keeping the commandments of God.

Keeping the commandments of God is what unifies us as a nation. We cannot unify under the guise of Christianity, nor under the so-called false democracy Deacon Malachi touched on. The only thing that will unify us is these scriptures, coming to understand who we are first, as the Israelites. America knows that; the white man knows that. That is why he pumps billions of dollars into religion and politics to keep the Israelites divided.

“Lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us.”

“Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” Like we have today: in today's society we have taskmasters over us.

“And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” We built Egypt: the Valley of Kings, those pyramids, those great cities. Once the Israelites left Egypt, not another pyramid popped up. If those Arabs are really the ancient Egyptians like they say, where are the great new cities? The same people that built up Egypt are the people that built up America and made America great.

The Most High raised up Moses while we were slaves in Egypt. Moses kept Jethro's flock at Horeb, “the mountain of God”, and “the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush”, and the bush “was not consumed.” When Moses turned aside to see, God called him out of the midst of the bush.

“Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.” The Most High expects humility of us, to come before him with a humble spirit. Moses was a great man in Egypt, second to Pharaoh, raised in all the customs of Egypt. God said, I don't want to hear all of that. Taking off the shoes was symbolic.

The Most High requires the same of us when we come into this truth. All the Christian garbage we learned: leave it outside. Islam: garbage, leave it outside. Nuwaubianism, Afrocentric, black power: it is all garbage. We must reform our minds as Israelites and meditate in these scriptures.
“I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.”

“I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters.” He came down to bring them “unto a land flowing with milk and honey.” That land is Jerusalem, but Jerusalem is a people first before it is an actual place. The gutter rats in Jerusalem now are not the real Jews; right now that land is Canaan. When Christ brings us back into the land, then it shall be Jerusalem.

The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites are the sons of Ham.

“I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” The Most High sees us being oppressed here in America, and he expects us to cry unto him the same way we did in Egypt. That is why the prayer before class asked for vengeance on our enemies. We are supposed to pray for that. The Christian church says turn the other cheek and pray for peace; where is that in the Bible? We are supposed to pray for the destruction of our enemies.
God sends Moses to Pharaoh to bring forth the children of Israel, and when Moses asks, “Who am I”, God answers, “Certainly I will be with thee.”

Moses asks what to say when they ask his name, and God answers, “I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” Who was speaking to Moses here? Christ.

precepts.why:
This is what the Most High requires when we come before him. “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God.” Sometimes we come with pride, with contention, acting like we know. You don't know a damn thing, because if you did, you would not have followed white Jesus.

“And be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.” Our brothers and sisters in the world don't consider that they are in evil, and often when they come into our sanctuaries it is the same thing: pride and contention, thinking they know much when they don't.

Keep thy foot means keep your mouth shut when you enter the house of God. Same thing he told Moses: put off thy shoes.
“Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” So the I AM that spoke to Moses out of the bush was Christ. Christ spoke directly to Moses.

sense.text:
Moses delivered us out of Egypt; that is what the Passover was for, the high holy day we just finished celebrating. Now we are in the wilderness.

“All our fathers.” Our fathers: a possessive noun. Read it right or you will get confounded by a Christian. Our fathers go through Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the Israelites. He is not the father of all nations. Yes, he created everybody, but he has a chosen, particular people, and that is the so-called Negroes and Hispanics, descendants of slaves, the Israelites.

“Under the cloud”: that cloud is the chariots of God, what the so-called white man calls UFOs, or now UAPs.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea.” That baptism is Moses teaching us the laws of God and also teaching us the gospel, teaching us about Christ, because he spoke with Christ, and Christ held him up in the mountain a long season. We think the gospel just happened when we get to the book of Matthew. No.
We “did all eat the same spiritual meat; and did all drink the same spiritual drink”, which we complained about. “For they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”
“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.”

“Now these things were our examples.” The things written aforetime were written for our learning. The brothers in the church of Corinth and in all the churches where we were scattered in Asia Minor had to learn the things written in foretime, and we are doing the same thing today. That is why Bishop always says the acts of the apostles continue. We learn from the example of our forefathers: “to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted” in the wilderness.

“Neither be ye idolaters.” Come up out of these religions and denominations, and not just religions: malice, guile, envy, adultery, fornication, lying, stealing, whatever has us in a stronghold. Anything you put before the Most High God is idolatry.

“The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Rose up to play means orgies, sex, fornication. That is what happened in the wilderness.

Paul expounds it in verse 8: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” The Most High is not playing. Twenty-three thousand souls gone in the blink of an eye, because they fell into their own lust and did not keep the commandments of God given to Moses.

“Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents. Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.”

That murmuring spirit is a heavy thing, and we see it throughout different IUIC congregations. Brothers and sisters take it lightly because it is only speech. It is more than speech. The brother or sister next to you can't hear you, but the angels are writing all of it down and reporting it right to God.

“Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples”: examples to us. It happened to them in their actions; they passed away, but it is an example for us not to walk in the same footsteps. “And they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.”

precepts.why:
Moses was teaching the Israelites the gospel. Christ speaks to Ezra of Moses: “where I held him by me a long season”, the forty days and forty nights on the mount.

“And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end.” Moses saw the beginning, the middle and the end of times; that is how he was able to write about it in the first five books. He was commanded: “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

“That thou lay up in thy heart the signs that I have shewed, and the dreams that thou hast seen, and the interpretations which thou hast heard: For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.” Moses even saw himself not entering into the promised land. He saw it, because he saw the beginning, middle and end.

So the baptism unto Moses in the cloud was Moses teaching the gospel of Christ that Christ had shown him.

sense.text:
We are reading the history of our forefathers in the wilderness and how rebellious we were. Although the Most High showed great signs and wonders, we were still stiff-necked, hard-headed people.

“Ah sinful nation.” We are a sinful nation, and we have to be honest and sincere with ourselves about that, even in our prayers. Don't go to the Most High acting like you are righteous when you are full of dead bones and sin and all manner of scum and guile. Open your mouth and confess to the Lord the things you are in the midst of and battling with. None of us is righteous; we are trying to be, but there is sin still in us.

“A people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin.

“They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why we are in captivity now. The so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity because it was prophesied in Deuteronomy 28: break my commandments, and these curses, verse 15 through 68, fall on you as a nation.

“They are gone away backward.” Many of our brothers and sisters are still moonwalking away from the Most High God. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

precepts.why:
This is why we are in need of a saviour. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ. “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden.” Heavy laden with what? We just read it in Isaiah: sin, a people laden with iniquity.

“And I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night's sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God: rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest Christ is talking about, but we have to come unto him.

sense.text: “And the Lord spake unto Moses.” Moses did not come up with this idea by himself; the instruction came from the Most High.

“Send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel.” This is the point, and where they lacked faith. Who was really fighting the fight? The Lord. He had already told them, I'm going to deliver these dusty Hamites into your hands, and they were still fearful and doubted, except for Caleb and Joshua.

“Every one a ruler among them.” These were not regular brothers. They were rulers, leaders, men of renown with a reputation, men that can lead other men.
“All those men were heads of the children of Israel.”
Among the names is Caleb the son of Jephunneh of the tribe of Judah, the same brother who would show faith when the rest showed fear.
“And they returned from searching of the land after forty days.” Forty days. Hold on to that number.

They showed the congregation the fruit of the land: “surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it.” They agreed with that part, because the Most High's promise was to bring them into a land flowing with milk and honey.

“Nevertheless the people be strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.” Verse 27 says the land is good; now in verse 28 you see doubt.

“And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” Caleb showed faith and courage: I don't give a damn about them damn dusty Hamites. I don't care how tall they are. The Most High said he is going to deliver our enemies into our hands.

“But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” The same men that were valiant, rulers and leaders, had doubt and fear. As Deacon Ithan always says, doubt and fear is Satan's playground.

They “brought up an evil report”: “we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.” They were shook to death of these Hamites, not understanding what the Most High had promised them.

“And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.” Now the spirit of fear jumped on everybody. These men were supposed to be rulers and leaders, and they put doubt and fear into all Israel.

“And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron.” There is that murmuring spirit again. They murmured against Moses and Aaron, but who were they truly murmuring against? The instruction came from the Most High: “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

“Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt!”

“And wherefore hath the Lord brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword, that our wives and our children should be a prey?” You mean our forefathers and foremothers really believed the Most High did all those miracles, all the curses and the power he showed to bring them out of Egypt, just to have them die? You see how simple and stupid we got. No different than today, like the dumb black woman in the video.

“Were it not better for us to return into Egypt?” When they were in captivity in Exodus 1, crying from their taskmasters, the Most High heard their cry. Now in the wilderness they want to go back to master. Harriet Tubman said she could have saved a thousand more if they had known they were slaves. Our people really want to stay here with master in Babylon, America: the same dumb thought our people had in the wilderness.

“Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.” They wanted to appoint a new leader. God appointed Moses and Aaron; they wanted somebody else who would give heed to their itching ears and do what they want.

“Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly.” This was repeated all through the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: they murmured and complained, and Moses always had to pray to the Most High for forgiveness and mercy. The Most High was not playing with us in the wilderness; a lot of people were put to death.

“How long will this people provoke me?” The Most High is showing long-suffering here. “And how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them?” He showed all these signs and they were moved by unbelief, complaining and wanting to go back to Pharaoh.
“I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.”
“The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression.” The Most High was very long-suffering with our forefathers in the wilderness.

Moses prays, “Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy”, and the Lord answers, “I have pardoned according to thy word.” That is how much the Most High loved the children of Israel, and Moses. Moses was the mediator between us and God, crying and praying unto God, and the Most High forgave us.

“Because all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness”: the plagues. “And have tempted me now these ten times.” These ten times are the countless acts of stubbornness of the children of Israel when we came out of Egypt. Write them down: the Red Sea, Marah, the wilderness of Sin, the manna hoarding, the Sabbath manna, Massah and Meribah, the golden calf, Taberah, Kibroth-hattaavah, and the tenth, the report of the spies.

precepts.why:
The first is at the Red Sea. “Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness?” They were complaining to Moses.

“Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.”

Number two, at Marah. “They could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter”, “And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?” They complained that the water was bitter.

Number three, the wilderness of Sin. “And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.” You notice a trend? It is going to be the same thing when Christ comes back, but Christ isn't playing games with us this time. He didn't play games back then either. This time it will be ten times worse, ten times more severe, ten times more strict. The next time we are saved out of this modern-day Egypt, Babylon the Great, America, the United Snakes of America, and Christ brings us into the wilderness, grace is finished. No more I should have, could have, would have.

“Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full.”

Number four, the manna hoarding. “And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.” Moses gave specific instructions. “Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses.” They said, the hell with you; we want to replace you anyway. That is the mindset of our people. “And it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.”

Number five, the Sabbath manna. “There went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none. And the Lord said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?”

“He giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days.” They were supposed to gather extra on the sixth day; the Most High gave them manna to lay up for two days. No, we are going to go out on the seventh day and get this manna, forgetting everything the Most High did in bringing us out of Egypt. We are a people of no gratitude at all.

Number six, at Massah and Meribah. “Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink.” To chide is to murmur, to be contentious, to go back and forth. “Wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?”

“They be almost ready to stone me.” The Lord had Moses smite “the rock in Horeb” and water came out of it, and Moses “called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying, Is the Lord among us, or not?”

Number seven, the golden calf. “Up, make us gods, which shall go before us.” That is the no gratitude. The Most High just showed all these wonderful plagues and destroyed your enemy, and now you want a god of silver, gold and wood, a god that can't talk. No different from our people who despise this truth and want to go back to Christianity and white Jesus, or run to the East to Mecca and pray to a damn cobblestone that can't talk back or answer prayers. Our people are foolish: dumber than an ox, dumber than a koala or a sloth. But through Christ's efforts we are going to be okay.

“For as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.” Look how disrespectful. Called him the damn devil. Aaron, the high priest, got real simple here, but it was out of fear. Aaron knew better as a high priest. He took the gold, the spoils we came out of Egypt with, and with the skill of a smith “fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf”; but it was the people who “said, These be thy gods, O Israel.”

“The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play”: in honour of this new pagan god they had orgies. “They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them.” “Behold, it is a stiffnecked people.” Yes, we are.

Number eight, Taberah. “And when the people complained, it displeased the Lord.” More complaining. “The fire of the Lord burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.” The Most High started burning people with fire, the same thing he is going to do in America.

“And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the Lord, the fire was quenched. And he called the name of the place Taberah.”

“The mixt multitude that was among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely.” About food: black people for you. “But now our soul is dried away: there is nothing at all, beside this manna.” Ungrateful. They complained about the manna.
Number nine, Kibroth-hattaavah: “because there they buried the people that lusted.”

sense.text: The tenth time is the report of the spies: the doubt and fear these people had. This was the final one; the Most High had enough.
“Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it.”

“But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land.” Caleb is the same brother who wanted to go into the land. He did not have doubt and fear.
“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” The murmuring against Moses and Aaron was murmuring against the Lord.
“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land.” Doubtless: that is the doubt and fear spoken of earlier. None enter, “save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.”
“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in.” The little ones went in. Those that were twenty and upward did not enter the land.
“And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.”

“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.” The spies searched the land forty days, and the Most High gave forty years: each day for a year. “In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.”

See how the Most High deals with numbers. He doesn't put things out there that are insignificant, though we might look at them that way. Everything in the Bible is significant. That is why we went the long way through this history.

“And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord”, forsook the Lord God of their fathers “which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods”, “and provoked the Lord to anger.”

“And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them”, so that they could not stand before their enemies. “Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil.”
“Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them.” The Most High heard our cries and raised up judges, the same way he raised up Moses.
“And yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but they went a whoring after other gods.” Still we would not listen to the Most High God, the same thing we did in the wilderness.

“For it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.” A pattern: Israel sins, we cry out, God delivers. Israel sins, we cry out, he delivers. It is the same thing as in the wilderness.

“When the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers.” That is why we are in need of a shepherd. We cannot be without a judge. When left to ourselves, we destroy ourselves. “They ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.”
“Because he had compassion on his people.” The Most High always had compassion on us.
“But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.”

He brought upon them “the king of the Chaldees.” In the time of Babylon the Babylonians destroyed the temple: “they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem.” If the temple is destroyed, what cannot take place? Sacrifice.

Those that escaped the sword went into captivity, “servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia”, “to fulfil threescore and ten years.”

So we could not sacrifice. We were always in captivity; that is why the prophet Jeremiah called Israel a homeborn slave. Even when the temple was up, many of us would not return to Jerusalem at the high holy days to atone for our sins. That is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice.

Fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen “until the carrying away into Babylon”, and fourteen “from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ.” We were always in slavery, without sacrifice, until Christ.
“And thou shalt call his name JESUS”, which means he saves: “for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people: the Israelites only. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

precepts.why: His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice.

“Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me.” That body was Christ. The sacrificial laws of animal sacrifice were only a preparation for what was to come, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ, dying only for the nation of Israel.

“In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in those sacrifices. They were temporary, to train us and prepare us for Christ.

“Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” The volume of the whole book, not just the New Testament. Christ is present in the Old Testament, and present before the Old Testament.

Christ was always the plan, brothers and sisters: the author, the executive producer, whatever title you want to give him. “All things were made by him”: principalities, the things you see in space, the worlds with an s. “And without him was not any thing made that was made.”

sense.text: “Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.”

“And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” The seventh day is not Sunday.

The number seven represents completion, perfection. Christ rested on the seventh day, and resting from servile work on the seventh day, the day of rest, is all symbolic of what is to come.

precepts.why: For those new online, the rules of the Sabbath: is congregating enough? No. There are laws that apply to the Sabbath day. “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work.” No working, no servile work on the Sabbath.

“To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.” Before Friday sundown, complete darkness, you are to lay up your food for the next day, because there is no cooking.

“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” That is not talking about turning on the heat because the house is freezing. It is talking about cooking: don't kindle a fire to cook. Stop following Amalek, these so-called Jewish people who are not the real Jews, adding to the law with their Talmud, their oral law.

“Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death.” Brothers coming out of different religions think the Sabbath day is for everyone. When Christ comes back, yes, everyone will be forced to keep it, and if they don't, we will break their heads wide open. But the Sabbath day was created for one group of people: the Israelites.

“Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel.” Not the Ammonites, not the white man: only the children of Israel.

sense.text: “To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.” This goes back to the same history of the wilderness just read; that is why we took the long way through it.
“But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?”

“And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.” What kept them out of the land was their unbelief.
“Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” Christ was taught back then, not just in the book of Matthew, but to our forefathers. “But the word preached did not profit them”, because they disobeyed Christ: “not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They were moved with unbelief.

“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” The rest of the seventh-day Sabbath is going into when Christ comes back and we reign with him. That is the true rest. “Although the works were finished from the foundation of the world”: paradise was already here.

“For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Notice that number keeps popping up: seven.

“If they shall enter into my rest.” In the wilderness the Most High also used the word rest: I'm going to bring you into the land, into rest. But did we truly rest in that land? There were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the damn Hamites we were fighting to get out of the land. The true rest is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back: rulership over our enemies.
“They to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief.” “To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.”

“For if Jesus had given them rest”: that Jesus is Joshua. Although Joshua was mighty and was smiting the Hamites, we didn't get true rest. The true rest is not going into the land; it is the kingdom of God on earth.
“There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison of our works to God's.

“Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest.” Labour, in pain; bring forth your works to enter into that rest, the kingdom. “Lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief”, the example of what we read in the wilderness.

precepts.why: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.” That paradise is for the Israelites; it is not talking about all nations. And there it is: rest is allowed, the rest that we which have believed enter into.

“The works were finished from the foundation of the world.” Before Christ said, the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here.

Ezra shows it: God “gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life”, “And thou leddest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was here before the earth came forth.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.” No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work: be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth. Labour in pain and bring forth your works, to enter into that rest.

“Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.” Your works are what will allow you to enter in through those gates.

To expound that rest: the seventh-day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for our resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is when we will really rest from servile work. After the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them.” The nations will be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them”, because they are our possession, “and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

“In the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, our fear, and the hard bondage we were made to serve.

“But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.” “One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years, and the true rest is the thousand years of rulership under Christ.

“I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”, the souls “which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image”, “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” That is the rest. The seventh-day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ.

sense.text: Seven represents completion, and here is something else seven does. “Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.” Seven times: completion.

“But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me.” He had pride: I have to go wash in the Jordan? The Jordan was muddy water to him. “Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?” “So he turned and went away in a rage.”
His servants said, “if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?”

After his servant spoke to him he humbled himself: “Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan”, completion in the river Jordan, “and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.”

Who allowed this to happen? Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ. Christ did the healing, using Elisha as the prophet. And Naaman was healed because he believed and he was obedient: his belief that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed it.

precepts.why:
“Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.” Putting away the evil of your doings is the true washing.

“Learn to do well.” Action, action, action: do well, not speak well. “Seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“Though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword.”

“Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts”: that is what the Most High desires. “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins, as Naaman's belief in the word of the prophet made him clean.

Naaman went down into the river Jordan to be cleansed, and John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins”, as written by Esaias: “Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went to John to be baptized in the Jordan, the same river Naaman had to dip in seven times: completion.

Christ himself referenced that history. Many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, “But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.” “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.”

sense.text: Seven also represents complete deliverance. “Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel”, and the Lord said, “See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour.”

Compass the city once, six days. “And seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams’ horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times.” Seven priests, seven trumpets, and on the seventh day, the Sabbath day, seven times around. Then “the wall of the city shall fall down flat.”

Joshua sends the seven priests with the seven trumpets before the ark, and commands the people, “Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout.” Once around each day: “so they did six days.”

“On the seventh day”, “only on that day they compassed the city seven times. And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city.”

On the seventh day, the Sabbath, because of their faith, the Most High brought down the walls of Jericho. Nothing is accidental with the Most High. He uses seven as a form of deliverance, and it represents totality, completion. That is what we have been reading from the beginning: the seventh-day rest, Naaman dipped seven times, and now the walls of Jericho compassed seven times with seven priests and seven trumpets.

precepts.why: “And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.” The seventh angel sounded the trump, and that brought forth completion: the same thing that happened when our forefathers compassed the walls of Jericho and the priests blew the seventh time.

sense.text: “Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” There are other appointed high holy days, like Purim, Nicanor and Hanukkah, but in Leviticus 23 there are seven, and every single one of them represents Jesus Christ.

“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest.” A weekly feast. The Sabbath's true meaning is rest: why God wants us to rest from servile work on the Sabbath, because ultimately that is what we will do in the kingdom. That rest means entering into the kingdom and ruling with Christ for a thousand years.

“These are the feasts of the Lord”, the annual feasts: “In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.” The Passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us.

precepts.why: “Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats.”

“Ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.” Christ was that lamb without blemish, the same as Exodus 12. And John the Baptist said of him, when he saw him coming, Behold the Lamb of God that taketh away the sin of the world.
“Neither shall ye break a bone thereof.” Those are the instructions on how to slaughter the lamb: don't break the bones thereof.
The prophecy about Christ: “He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.”

The Jews besought Pilate “that their legs might be broken”, “for that sabbath day was an high day.” The soldiers “brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs”, fulfilling the prophecy of Psalms 34:20. Christ is the Passover lamb.

The lambs without blemish were raised in Bethlehem and slaughtered in Jerusalem, the same as Jesus Christ. “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.” Christ was born in Bethlehem.

The high priests given charge over the unblemished lambs had them wrapped in cloths and brought to Jerusalem for sacrifice from Migdal Eder in Bethlehem. Migdal Eder means tower of the flock, the same tower of the flock in Micah the fourth chapter, the eighth verse. So Jesus, born in Bethlehem and wrapped in cloths, was brought to Jerusalem at Passover, where he offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins.

Joseph went “unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem”, “To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.” To be taxed together you have to be married, with papers, filing jointly.

“And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes”: the same thing our forefathers did with the lambs they brought to Jerusalem, fulfilling prophecy. So we know Christ was our Passover.

sense.text:
“The feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.” There is that seven again.

The unleavened bread represents Christ, his sinless life without leaven. We know the history of why it was unleavened: the Most High wanted us to hurry up and leave Egypt, with no time to bake bread. But it also goes into Christ's unleavened life, sinless and blameless.
“In the first day ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.”

precepts.why: “I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger.” Christ is the bread of life.

“Purge out therefore the old leaven”: that leaven is sin. “That ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us.” Christ was that unleavened bread that laid his life down for the children of Israel.

sense.text: The Sabbath, the Passover, unleavened bread: that is three. Number four is the feast of firstfruits. “Seven sabbaths shall be complete: Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days.”
“Two wave loaves”, “they are the firstfruits unto the Lord.”

precepts.why: “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.” Christ is the firstfruits. “For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming.” The same promise is to us, if we believe and keep the commandments and the faith of Christ.

“Ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” The redemption of the body we used to have when we were in the heavens with Christ. We are supposed to be the firstfruits, the crème de la crème, the best of the best, if we repent in Christ.
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures”, if we follow after Christ's example.

“These are they which were not defiled with women”: not defiled with philosophy, not defiled with doctrine, and not defiled with literal women. “These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.”

sense.text: Number five, the feast of trumpets: “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.” We blow the trumpet because we were commanded to, on the new moons and on our high holy days; but this too is a representation of Christ.
“Ye shall do no servile work therein: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.”

precepts.why: “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” The elect is only Israel, not all nations. We were scattered from one end of heaven to the other, and that tells you who the children of God are: the only people scattered from one end of the earth to the other are the so-called blacks and Hispanics, the Israelites.

That trumpet is not a flute or a soft sound. When Christ comes back, everybody is going to fear. “And the Lord shall be seen over them, and his arrow shall go forth as the lightning: and the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south.” This is when we conquer the nations.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones.” We are going to devour all these nations, put them under our feet, and break them in half.

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” That is some beautiful stuff right there.

“And the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man heareth, they shall be suddenly afraid.” That is how you know it is not a flute or a harmonica or any instrument you can think of. That trumpet is a frightening sound.

sense.text: “Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls.” Christ was that atonement.

precepts.why:
“By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament”: the new covenant. “And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death.” The priests died. “But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood. Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost.”

Christ is the true high priest, in whom there was no death. That is how he is able to atone for our sins continually.

“But by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” That blood was given for atonement, and he died only once, for us, the Israelites.

“How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God”, blameless, with no sin, “purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?”

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”, just as Moses was the mediator for us when we came out of Egypt, that “they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance”, if we believe.

“For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.” For the testament to come to fruition and be valid, the testator had to die; that is why Christ had to die. “For a testament is of force after men are dead”, because while you are alive it could change. “Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood”: blood had to be spilled for the first covenant of animal sacrifice too.

“Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood.” Propitiation means atonement. God sent Christ “to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God.”

“And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.” That world is the scattered Israelites, all Israel, that they may have time to repent. It is not talking about all nations.

Christ is the new high priest. “For in the long garment was the whole world”: Aaron the high priest had the whole world in his long garment, the ephod, with a stone for each tribe. The world on Aaron's chest represented Israel, not the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Hittites, the Perizzites or the Ishmaelites. Only the Israelites.

“And in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven.”

sense.text: “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.” Another word for tabernacles is Succoth, booths, and it means to dwell.

precepts.why: “And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.” He pitched his tent amongst us. Christ walked and dwelt amongst us.
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” The Jews got simple: “Forty and six years was this temple in building.” “But he spake of the temple of his body”: the tabernacle.

Christ came “by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands”, because his body was the temple, and “by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.”

“Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them.” That is what tabernacle means: to dwell. Dwell with whom? The Israelites. “And they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.”

All seven high holy days of Leviticus 23 represent Jesus Christ. He isn't the God of the Ishmaelites, he isn't the God of the Arabs, he isn't the God of the white man. He is the God of Israel only.

sense.text: “Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars.” Christ and wisdom are one and the same, interchangeable, because Christ is the ultimate, complete wisdom, and seven represents completion. Who does this wisdom with the seven pillars pertain to? Christ.

precepts.why: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.” This is Christ, the wisdom of chapter 9.

“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: that is Christ.

“And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”, one; “the spirit of wisdom”, two; “and understanding”, three; “the spirit of counsel”, four; “and might”, five; “the spirit of knowledge”, six; “and of the fear of the Lord”, seven. Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had, representing complete spiritual perfection. That is what Christ operated in.

sense.text:
Now the flip side: the devil. Cain slew his brother, and complained that whoever found him would slay him. “Whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.” How could vengeance be taken sevenfold for Cain? Because Cain was the ultimate murderer.

Cain came back as Esau. Look at his vengeance, how he does the earth, what he did to the people of this land, what he is doing right now to the Ishmaelites in the land of Palestine. His vengeance cannot be quenched; he is all about murder and bloodshed to the epitome. That is what that seven represents. Every September 11 he says he shall never forget, but he tells the so-called blacks to forget about slavery. The damn Amalekites still talk about the Holocaust, shoving it down people's throats and using it as a means to murder the Palestinians.

“And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.”
Lamech, Cain's great-great-great-great-grandson: “for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.” He killed a man.

“If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” Seventy and sevenfold: complete vengeance, total and utter vengeance. Through regeneration we come back, and it would not be surprising if Lamech were Cain all over again; he walks in the same footsteps. Damn devil.

That is why Sirach says never trust thine enemy. You can't trust this man. You think he forgot how we did him under King David, put them in garrisons and pushed them off mountains? You think he forgot that we pushed them into the wilderness and they became the wildlings during the Dark Ages? He hasn't forgotten. He is still acting out his vengeance on the so-called blacks and Hispanics.

Patrice Lumumba is the example: one of the officers responsible for his death poured acid on his chopped-up body, kept his gold tooth, and laughed about it; his family kept it until Belgium returned it in a coffin to the Congo. The same thing they did with Nat Turner, passing his skull down as an heirloom, a trophy. These people are the damn devil the Bible speaks of.

precepts.why: That is the perpetual hatred. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.” Perpetual hatred is great, ongoing, fiery hatred.

“For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.” Forever: perpetual. He hates our guts.

“For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.”

So Lamech's seventy and seven was complete vengeance, perpetual hatred: that is what Esau is driven with.

sense.text: Now the flip side of Lamech: “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?”

“I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ offers boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to make sure he did the same.

Why does Christ use seventy times seven? We know seven represents completion. The same way Christ forgave us when we were without sacrifice and without mercy: he came and forgave all our adulteries, fornication, lying and stealing, through Assyria, Babylon, Persia, America, when we were scattered in Africa in the Dark Ages doing all sorts of wicked things. Christ forgave all of that. That is why he said seventy times seven.

Christ didn't just put numbers out there. When Christ spoke, the Pharisees would walk away and an hour later realize he had been cutting them. Seventy times seven is four hundred and ninety, and that number is in Daniel.

precepts.why: “If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.” That brother is the children of thy people. “And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.”

“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness”, which Christ offers, “humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”, if they repent.

“Forbearing one another”, as Christ forbears us, “and forgiving one another.” Some of us need to pray for that. Some of you can't forgive anything and hold on to grudges like there's no tomorrow. Imagine if Christ held grudges against us: we wouldn't be here. You would be in hell with your white Jesus, your Islam, your sins. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ and his boundless mercies toward us.

“Even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.”

sense.text: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”: seventy times seven, four hundred and ninety years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

“From the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem”: that is Nehemiah. “Unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ. “The street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times”: the time of Nehemiah, who had to rebuild the walls in troublous times because the heathen didn't want to see us rebuild.

“Shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: that prince is Titus. “The end thereof shall be with a flood”: 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

“In the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “And for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate.”

So you get four hundred and ninety years, the prophecy of Christ coming and being cut off for the children of Israel, completing that perfection through Christ. We needed that mercy. We could not sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, so we needed Christ.

precepts.why: “And to anoint the most Holy” is talking about Christ: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.”

“And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” Those armies are the Roman armies: the people of the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary in Daniel 9:26.

“We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree. Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel.”

Now we understand what he told Peter in Matthew 18 about seventy times seven: I want you to forgive your brother seventy times seven because I forgave you seventy times seven, for all those captivities where we couldn't sacrifice, in the midst of sin, going from one captivity to the next. The only reason we are here is Christ. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

“These are they which came out of great tribulation”, the Israelites, “and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” That sacrifice, Christ dying for us, is the only thing that can bring us through to perfection.

“For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.” Sinning wilfully is coming up, learning this truth, and going back into the world saying, forget the laws, put me back to sleep. Christ will put you to sleep, and when you wake up it will be in that hellfire.

“He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God”: how much more punishment for taking for granted the body and blood and sacrifice of our Messiah who laid down his life for us, to continue in your wickedness and forsake this truth.

“Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.”

“For the love of Christ constraineth us”: it puts a brake on our impulses. “That if one died for all, then were all dead: And that he died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.”

So we owe Christ a major price. Christ is the complete perfection, brothers and sisters.
